hero.body: OperonIQ brings together senior practitioners across business transformation, process redesign, data architecture, enterprise platforms, intelligent automation and AI — unified into a single delivery model that connects strategic intent to measurable operational change.

conviction.title: Real transformation starts before the technology.
conviction.p1: Before any platform is selected or AI agent deployed, the business process must be understood, redesigned and owned by the people who run it. Technology layered onto poorly defined or fragmented processes does not create capability — it creates complexity at scale.
conviction.p2Bold: business process redesign as the foundation of every engagement
conviction.p2Suffix: . We map how work actually flows, identify where it breaks down, and design the target operating model before recommending a single tool or platform. This is not a discovery phase — it is the work.
calloutItems: Map current-state processes, decision points and friction across functions
Design the target operating model with clear ownership and value linkage
Identify where automation, AI agents and data can enhance redesigned processes
Validate change impact and align leadership before deployment begins

why.title: The market fragments what organisations need whole.
why.p1: Most advisory firms are organised around a single discipline — business consulting, data engineering, Microsoft platforms, or AI strategy. Clients are left to coordinate between providers, reconcile competing recommendations, and absorb the gaps that form between specialisms.
why.p2: OperonIQ was created to close those gaps. Our practitioners hold depth across business, data, platform and AI — and our delivery model is designed so those disciplines reinforce each other rather than operating in sequence.
why.unify: OperonIQ unifies all of them into one integrated transformation model.

s01-01.name: Agentic Readiness Assessment
s01-01.challenge: Leaders lack a clear picture of where autonomous AI agents can safely and profitably operate inside their organisation.

s01-02.name: Business Transformation Assessment
s01-02.challenge: Organisations face pressure to modernise but struggle to connect technology investments to measurable business outcomes.

s01-03.name: AI Workforce Strategy
s01-03.challenge: Executives need a credible plan for integrating digital workers alongside their human workforce without disrupting culture or productivity.

s01-04.name: Executive Advisory
s01-04.challenge: C-suite leaders need trusted, vendor-neutral guidance to navigate rapidly evolving AI capabilities and competitive dynamics.

02.name: Modern Work
02.conviction: Enable people to collaborate, decide and execute faster.

s02-01.name: Microsoft 365 Strategy
s02-01.challenge: Organisations have invested in Microsoft 365 but struggle to realise value beyond email and basic file storage.
outcomes: Unified adoption strategy across M365 workloads

s02-02.name: Copilot Readiness Programme
s02-02.challenge: Deploying Microsoft Copilot without preparing people, processes, content and governance leads to low adoption and wasted investment.
outcomes: High Copilot adoption from day one

s02-03.name: Teams & SharePoint Governance
s02-03.challenge: Ungoverned Teams and SharePoint environments create sprawl, duplication and security risk as organisations scale.

s02-04.name: Knowledge Management
s02-04.challenge: Critical organisational knowledge is locked in email, in people's heads, or in unstructured content that AI cannot reliably use.

03.name: Data & Analytics
03.conviction: Turn fragmented data into trusted intelligence.

s03-01.name: Data Platform Readiness
s03-01.challenge: Fragmented, legacy data platforms block AI adoption and create bottlenecks that slow decision-making across the enterprise.

s03-02.name: Analytics Modernisation
s03-02.challenge: Dashboards report what happened — executives need forward-looking intelligence to act ahead of the curve.
outcomes: Shift from descriptive to predictive analytics

s03-03.name: Data Governance
s03-03.challenge: Without clear data ownership and quality controls, AI systems inherit the errors and biases of their underlying data.
tags: ML anomaly detection on data quality

s03-04.name: AI Data Foundations
s03-04.challenge: Most enterprise data is not in the shape or quality required to fuel production AI and LLM workloads.
outcomes: Curated datasets ready for LLM fine-tuning and RAG

04.name: Business Applications
04.conviction: Connect CRM, ERP and operational workflows.

s04-01.name: Dynamics 365 CRM Advisory
s04-01.challenge: CRM implementations often fail to reflect how the business actually sells, services or retains customers.
outcomes: CRM aligned to customer journey reality
Higher adoption across sales and service teams
Cleaner data feeding AI and reporting

s04-02.name: Business Central Optimisation
s04-02.challenge: Finance and operations teams work around Business Central rather than through it, creating manual workarounds and data gaps.
outcomes: ERP positioned to support AI agents

s04-03.name: Customer Journey Transformation
s04-03.challenge: Disconnected systems create fragmented customer experiences that damage retention and make AI-assisted service impossible.

05.name: Automation & Agentic AI
05.conviction: Design digital workforces that accelerate execution.

s05-01.name: Agent Factory
s05-01.challenge: Organisations want to deploy AI agents quickly but lack the reusable tooling and standards to do so at scale.
outcomes: Rapid agent provisioning in days not months
deliverables: Python agent SDK and template repository

s05-02.name: Multi-Agent Architectures
s05-02.challenge: Complex workflows require networks of specialised agents that collaborate, delegate and verify each other's outputs.
outcomes: Robust error recovery and fault tolerance
Transparent audit trails across agent hops
deliverables: Integration test suite and observability stack

s05-03.name: Intelligent Automation Programmes
s05-03.challenge: Traditional RPA programmes plateau once simple rules run out — intelligent automation adds judgement to exception-heavy processes.
outcomes: Automation that learns and adapts over time

s05-04.name: Digital Workforce Enablement
s05-04.challenge: Deploying agents in isolation creates point solutions — scaling to a true digital workforce requires shared infrastructure and governance.
outcomes: Coordinated fleet of agents operating end-to-end
Measurable capacity gains in target functions

s05-05.name: AI Agent Design
s05-05.challenge: Without thoughtful design, AI agents fail to earn user trust, behave inconsistently, or optimise for the wrong outcomes.
outcomes: Agents that are intuitive, reliable and safe
Clear scope, persona and escalation paths

06.name: Governance & Quality

s06-01.name: Responsible AI Governance
s06-01.challenge: Boards and regulators demand evidence that AI systems are fair, transparent and safe — few organisations have the frameworks to prove it.
outcomes: Bias detection and mitigation in place
deliverables: Model cards for all production models

s06-02.name: Quality Engineering
s06-02.challenge: AI systems require testing approaches beyond traditional QA — covering model behaviour, prompt robustness and integration reliability.

s06-03.name: Platform Governance
s06-03.challenge: As AI platforms grow, ungoverned sprawl leads to cost overruns, security gaps and inconsistent user experience.
tags: ML anomaly detection on usage patterns

s06-04.name: Transformation Advisory Retainer
s06-04.challenge: Sustaining transformation momentum requires ongoing expert capacity that most internal teams cannot maintain alone.
outcomes: Rapid response to emerging AI developments
Alignment between AI and business strategy maintained
deliverables: Monthly health checks and model performance reviews

NexIQSystem:
You are NexIQ, the intake assistant for OperonIQ - a senior-led boutique consultancy specialising in business transformation, data, automation and agentic AI. Your only job is to gather initial context from a prospective client so that when a senior OperonIQ practitioner follows up, they are fully prepared.

Tone: direct, warm, professional. No filler. No corporate speak. No emojis. Sound like a senior consultant, not a chatbot. Never say "Great!" or "Absolutely!" or "Of course!". No hollow affirmations.

Respond only in English, regardless of the language the visitor uses.

You have already introduced yourself and asked what brought them to OperonIQ. Now ask these questions one at a time in order:
1. Which area of the business is most affected - process, data, technology, people, or a combination?
2. Roughly how large is the organisation?
3. Is there a specific timeline or trigger driving this?
4. What does a successful outcome look like in the next 6-12 months?

After the fourth answer: thank them briefly, confirm a senior OperonIQ team member will follow up within one business day, and ask for their name and email so we can route the conversation to the right person. Then close warmly and concisely - no more questions after that.

Hard rules:
- One question per message only
- Keep each message under 3 sentences
- Acknowledge their answer briefly before asking the next - never repeat verbatim
- Never offer advice, analysis or service descriptions
- Extract the following from the conversation and include them as a JSON block at the very end of your final message (after you have collected name and email), on its own line, with no other text after it:
  SUMMARY_JSON:{"trigger":"...","area":"...","size":"...","timeline":"...","outcome":"...","name":"...","email":"..."}
